lines: One input channel of the Chained Mixer, with a fader, pan, mute, solo and two aux sends; it has no output of its own and feeds the Master beside it
Sets the level sent to the aux 1 bus, taken after the fader, off at the bottom and 0dB at the top
Sets the level sent to the aux 2 bus, taken after the fader, off at the bottom and 0dB at the top
Places the signal across the stereo field; with one input patched it pans, 3dB down in the centre, and with both patched it balances the two sides, unattenuated in the centre
Sets the channel level, silent at the bottom, 0dB at the marked position and 12dB at the top
Drops every channel that is not soloed out of the mix; a channel that is both soloed and muted is muted
Silences this channel
The left input, or the only input if this jack alone is patched; polyphonic channels are summed to one before mixing
The right input; with this jack alone patched the channel runs mono from it
Note — this module produces no sound by itself: it needs a Chained Mixer Master in the same unbroken run of Chained Mixer modules, and the audio comes out of the Master
Note — up to 16 channels feed one Master; counting from the left, a seventeenth and beyond is switched off and shows no number on its panel
Note — the panel carries no lettering of its own; the words AUX1, AUX2, PAN/BAL, 0dB, SOLO and MUTE are printed on the Master panel and run across the whole row
Note — mute and solo do not interact, so a channel can be left in both at once, in which case it is silent

ChainMixerChannel.notes: The fader curve is a table in src/common/Faders.cpp:22-36, running from -144dB at the bottom through 0dB at 0.746 of travel to +12dB at the top; the aux sends are a squared curve topping out at 0dB (Faders.cpp:244-249). Sets the overall level of the aux 2 send bus, off at the bottom and 0dB at the top
Sets the level at the outputs, silent at the bottom, 0dB at the marked position and 12dB at the top
Silences both outputs
The left side of the mix, one channel; with this jack alone patched it carries the whole mix summed to mono
The right side of the mix, one channel; with this jack alone patched it carries the whole mix summed to mono

Note — the lettering down the left of this panel, AUX1, AUX2, PAN/BAL, 0dB, SOLO and MUTE, names the controls of the Channel modules in the row, not controls of this module

ChainMixerAux.notes: ChainMixerAux.cpp:36-39 calls configParam(ParamSolo1, ...) twice and configParam(ParamMute1, ...) twice, never ParamSolo2 or ParamMute2. Two consequences, both visible in the installed build's census: the AUX 1 solo and mute buttons carry the names Solo AUX 2 and Mute AUX 2, and the AUX 2 solo and mute buttons have no ParamQuantity at all, so Rack's ParamWidget refuses to drag them and they stay at zero. The maker's manual describes AUX 2 solo and mute as working.

lines: A stereo chorus built from up to four modulated delay voices, each with its left and right sides a quarter cycle apart
Sets the speed of the internal LFOs from 1Hz to 10Hz; turned fully down the LFOs stop and the readout reads External Modulation Only
Sets how far the delay is swept, reaching about a semitone of pitch change at 100%
Filters the wet signal: turned left a lowpass falls from 22000Hz to 500Hz, turned right a highpass rises from 30Hz to 1000Hz, and in the centre neither is in the way
Chooses how many of the four voices run, 1 to 4; above one, the internal LFOs are detuned a few per cent against each other
Crossfades dry against wet on a constant-power curve, 0% to 100%
Scales the RATE control voltage, -100% to 100%, before it is added to the RATE knob; at zero the RATE input is out of circuit
Scales the DEPTH control voltage, -100% to 100%, before it is added to the DEPTH knob; at zero the DEPTH input is out of circuit
Scales the TONE control voltage, -100% to 100%, before it is added to the TONE knob; at zero the TONE input is out of circuit
Scales the WET control voltage, -100% to 100%, before it is added to the WET knob; at zero the WET input is out of circuit
The left audio input, with polyphonic channels summed to one; patched alone it feeds both sides 4.5dB down
The right audio input, with polyphonic channels summed to one; patched alone it feeds both sides 4.5dB down

External modulation of the first voice, 10V either way for the full sweep; a cable of eight or more channels here instead drives all eight circuits, channels 1 to 4 the left sides and 5 to 8 the right
External modulation of one voice, 10V either way for the full sweep; a second channel on the same cable modulates the right side of that voice on its own
Added to the RATE knob through the RATE attenuverter; 0 to 10V at 100% covers the whole knob, and the External Modulation Only position cannot be reached this way
Added to the DEPTH knob through the DEPTH attenuverter; 0 to 10V at 100% covers the whole 1% to 100% range
Added to the TONE knob through the TONE attenuverter, centred on 5V, so 0V and 10V reach the two ends at 100%
Added to the WET knob through the WET attenuverter; 0 to 10V at 100% covers the whole 0% to 100% range
The left output, one channel; with both outputs patched the two sides are modulated a quarter cycle apart, and with one alone the chorus runs mono
The right output, one channel; with both outputs patched the two sides are modulated a quarter cycle apart, and with one alone the chorus runs mono
Note — the audio path inside is one channel per side: polyphonic cables into the audio inputs are summed before processing and both outputs carry a single channel
Note — while the internal LFOs run, external modulation is halved and added to them; with RATE turned fully down the MODULATION inputs are the only thing moving the delays
Note — moving RATE in or out of the External Modulation Only position jumps the delay and can click, so it is not a good target for automation

StereoChorus.notes: The maker's four input names are spelled Moduulation in the source (StereoChorus.cpp:129-132), so that is what the tooltips read; the panel prints MODULATION. MODULATION inputs 2, 3 and 4 are polyphonic only in the sense that a second channel is read for the right side of that voice; further channels are ignored. The eight-channel mode belongs to input 1 alone and needs eight or more channels regardless of how many voices are selected.

lines: A rotating speaker effect: one input is split into two or three bands, each band fed to a speaker turning at its own speed, and picked up by a pair of virtual microphones
Adds a second treble horn, turning a little faster with a shorter ramp so the two horns drift apart; changing it can click
Sets how long the treble horn takes to reach speed, 0 to 12 seconds; slowing down takes about a quarter longer than speeding up
Sets the treble horn's speed in fast mode, 30 to 600 revolutions per minute
Sets the treble horn's speed in slow mode, 10 to 260 revolutions per minute
Switches the crossover from two-way, splitting at 800Hz, to three-way with a midrange speaker, splitting at 250Hz and 2000Hz; changing it can click
Sets how long the midrange speaker takes to reach speed, 0 to 12 seconds; slowing down takes about a quarter longer than speeding up
Sets the midrange speaker's speed in fast mode, 30 to 600 revolutions per minute
Sets the midrange speaker's speed in slow mode, 10 to 260 revolutions per minute
Sets how long the bass speaker takes to reach speed, 0 to 12 seconds; slowing down takes about a quarter longer than speeding up
Sets the bass speaker's speed in fast mode, 30 to 600 revolutions per minute
Sets the bass speaker's speed in slow mode, 10 to 260 revolutions per minute
Calls for slow rotation while it is latched on; a call for fast from anywhere overrides it
Calls for fast rotation while it is latched on, overriding any call for slow
Sets the distance from the microphones to the circle the speakers turn on, 0.1 to 1 metre; closer gives a deeper level sweep and a wider stereo image, and the audio delay does not change with it
Sets the angle between the left and right microphones, 60 to 180 degrees, the widest giving a ping-pong effect at close distances, though the manual gives the minimum as 90 degrees
The signal to be rotated, with polyphonic channels summed to one
Calls for slow rotation while it is above 1V
Calls for fast rotation while it is above 1V, overriding any call for slow
Sets rotation speed directly, 0V to 10V giving none to the full fast speed of every band; with a cable here the slow and fast buttons and inputs are ignored and their lamps go out
Takes rotation from a modulation wheel: below 3.3V stopped, above 3.3V slow, above 6.7V fast
The left microphone, one channel; with this jack alone patched it carries the mono pickup
The right microphone, one channel; with this jack alone patched it carries the mono pickup
Note — the buttons, the SLOW and FAST inputs and the WHEEL input are combined as a logical or, and fast beats slow wherever both are called for
Note — with only one output patched the module works one microphone position, so there is no stereo movement to hear
Note — there is no dry-wet control and no amplifier or speaker emulation; the output is the rotated signal alone
